messages:
amy_support: Heads-up — Acme escalated a rerank issue (INC-12345). They say scores are weird: some >1, one candidate came back as NaN. They copied the example from our Console/cURL docs. Pasting the customer cURL they ran:

amy_support: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -d '{"query": "best restaurants", "candidates": ["Chez Marie", "La Plaza"] }'
```

amy_support: They said the console UI returns the expected scores but their cURL returns very different numbers and a NaN for the second candidate. They also hit a 413 once while trying a 5000-item payload.

maria_eng: Thanks — assigning to eng to investigate. Quick Q: which endpoint variant did they use? /v1/rerank or /v1/rerank:stream?

amy_support: /v1/rerank (non-stream). Customer included response snippet: ```json
{
  "results": [
    {"candidate":"Chez Marie","score":1.234},
    {"candidate":"La Plaza","score":NaN}
  ]
}
```

raj_docs: I pulled their request from the support logs. Looks like they followed the cURL snippet in the public docs which is inconsistent with the Console example. Docs cURL shows a single JSON object body, console sends newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) per item for batching. That mismatch could cause parsing code to pick the wrong branch and return uninitialized scores for some candidates. Also I noticed the docs cURL example is missing the Content-Type header.

raj_docs: Problematic example in docs: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
  -d '{"query": "best restaurants", "candidates": ["Chez Marie", "La Plaza",], }'
```

raj_docs: Issues: trailing comma in array/object, no Content-Type, and example body formatted as a single JSON object while Console sends NDJSON for batched rerank requests. I'll prepare a docs PR.

maria_eng: Good find. From the runtime side, two things can produce NaN: 1) parse error that results in empty candidate text (we compute a score on token embeddings -> unexpected empty -> NaN), 2) a casting issue when the client passes `score` as a string and our serializer sees "NaN" literal. Also >1 scores are possible if customer is interpreting the raw similarity dot-product instead of normalized probability. We need to make semantics explicit: rerank returns a raw relevance score (unbounded float, higher is better) unless you request normalized scores via ?normalize=true.

viktor_sre: Also saw the 413 — request body size limit is 2MB for the hosted rerank endpoint by default. Console batches requests and uses streaming / chunked encoding, which stays under limits. The customer's single JSON array of 5000 candidates pushed the body over the limit. Recommend we document the 2MB limit and show chunked/NDJSON examples.

amy_support: OK — action items: 1) raj_docs: update cURL examples (headers, remove trailing commas, give NDJSON and JSON-array variants, show chunking). 2) maria_eng: add short note in API reference about score semantics + normalize param. 3) viktor_sre: confirm 2MB limit wording and suggest server-side 413 messaging improvement. I'll reply to customer with repro steps and workarounds.

raj_docs: Working on PR now. Proposed corrected cURL examples: single-request JSON array variant and NDJSON chunked variant — both with explicit Content-Type. Example NDJSON chunked: ```bash
# NDJSON (recommended for large batches)
echo '{"query":"best restaurants","candidates":["Chez Marie"]}' | sed -e 's/}\n/{\n/' | \
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' \
    --data-binary @-
```

raj_docs: Example small-batch JSON (Content-Type: application/json): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '[{"query":"best restaurants","candidates":["Chez Marie","La Plaza"]}]'
```

maria_eng: Those look good. I'll add a note in the reference: "score is raw relevance (dot-product) by default; use ?normalize=true to return scores in [0,1]." Also will add defensive parsing so an incoming single-object body is handled consistently and we error with 400 for malformed JSON (trailing commas) instead of returning NaN. That should stop this class of customer confusion.

viktor_sre: I'll open a small infra ticket to improve 413 messaging so it suggests chunking/NDJSON + give the 2MB limit value.

deploybot: Scheduled docs deployment to staging at 2026-03-16T02:00Z (docs PR #2789).

amy_support: I told Acme the immediate workaround: 1) use the NDJSON example or split candidate list into multiple smaller requests, 2) include Content-Type header, 3) retry after removing trailing commas. Asked them to re-run and paste request/response if still broken.

amy_support: Customer re-ran with corrected NDJSON and got expected numeric scores (no NaN). Closing INC-12345 once docs PR merges.

raj_docs: PR merged to main and deployed to staging. I'll follow up once prod deploy is confirmed.

maria_eng: I'll follow up with a small change to error handling + unit test to catch trailing-comma parsing.

viktor_sre: Infra note created: INFRA-559 (improve 413 messaging).

amy_support: Great work team — thanks. I'll mark this resolved in the ticket and send the paste of the fixed request/response to Acme for confirmation. :thumbsup:
